title: Observation of non-adiabatic non-Abelian braiding of matter waves
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75085-7

Non-Abelian braiding is a fundamental mechanism for implementing topological quantum computation. Here, the authors propose and demonstrate a quantum simulation of non-adiabatic non-Abelian braiding operation using a Bose Einstein condensate, realizing fast non-Abelian manipulation of matter waves.

title: Kat5 deficiency in alveolar type II cells licenses STAT6-driven glycolytic reprogramming and pulmonary fibrosis
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75317-w

Pulmonary fibrosis is a fatal lung disease driven by epithelial injury and metabolic shifts, yet their link is unclear. Here, the authors show that Kat5 acetylates STAT6 to limit fibrosis, and restoring Kat5 in epithelial cells alleviates fibrosis, revealing promising therapeutic targets.

title: Zeolitic isolated protonic acid sites-mediated NH<sub>3</sub> storage for robust NO<sub>x</sub> removal
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75294-0

Controlling nitrogen oxide emissions needs catalysts that work across harsh conditions. This study separates ammonia storage from reaction sites in oxide-zeolite hybrids, enabling stable, selective removal over a wide temperature range.

title: A low-temperature, water-free fabrication route to Mg-based micro thermoelectric coolers for thermal management
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75165-8

This study reports Mg-based micro thermoelectric coolers fabricated via a low-temperature process, achieving high cooling performance and enabling a scalable, sustainable alternative to conventional Bi2Te3-based devices for thermal management.

title: The Bipartisan infrastructure law’s impact on drinking water funding for disadvantaged communities
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74287-3

This study shows how U.S. states changed definitions of disadvantaged communities after the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and how these shifts affect which communities qualify for water funding and the equity ofallocations.

title: Fluid-mediated nuclearity control in heterogeneous polyolefin catalysis
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75099-1

The nuclearity of active sites in heterogeneous Ziegler–Natta catalysts plays a key role in determining polyolefin microstructure yet remains difficult to control during polymerization. Here, the authors use a liquid-containing polymerization strategy to induce dinuclear titanium species via periodic wetting–drying of n-hexane, enabling polymer microstructure control without altering catalyst composition.

title: Structure-guided reprogramming of DELLA turnover for a sustainable Green Revolution in rice
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75068-8

By structure-guided engineering of DELLA to modulate its degradation, Xue et al. break the long-standing yield-fertilizer dependency trade-off, achieving improved nitrogen-use efficiency and grain yield beyond conventional Green Revolution varieties.

title: Chemical intuition on bond-dissociation energies as an emergent ability of universal machine-learning interatomic potentials
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74919-8

Interatomic potentials generated by machine learning can model atomic-scale systems, but it remains unclear how they acquire chemical understanding. Here, the authors demonstrate how representations of binding energy emerge in scalable models.
